criteria.name: Hook strength
criteria.notes: First paragraph (~216 chars) names Curtis Thayer, his role, and the concrete decision (refuting the FERC tie-in claim as 'dead wrong') before the fold. Decision is the hook, not the bio. Docked slightly because the block is dense rather than a clean two-line punch.

criteria.name: Subject + decision load-bearing for AK
criteria.notes: Thayer's accountability is not soft; he owns the refutation outright. Consequence names sector (energy/AI infrastructure), dollar figure ($400M PowerLink), affected actors (DeepGreen, Kenai Peninsula stakeholders, future filers), and timeframe (Sept 4 comment window). Docked one tier because the decision is a reactive public correction rather than a capital, procurement, or funding allocation.

criteria.name: Subject identification fidelity
criteria.notes: Full name, title ('CEO and Executive Director'), org (AEA), and explicit Anchorage tie all match desk_dossier.json exactly. No invented biographical detail.

criteria.name: Decision specificity + primary-source
criteria.notes: What/when/binary all explicit and sharp, decision dated 2026-08-19, in-window under the 60-day override. Primary source (Anchorage Daily News) named inline. Corroboration present but implicit: the post uses Federal Register-sourced detail to corroborate the underlying filing but never surfaces that Thayer's rebuttal is single-sourced to ADN.

criteria.name: Structural read
criteria.notes: Takes a genuine, earned position ('He chose refutation, and it was the right call') and then names the real, proportionate tension (Chugach's appetite for large loads vs. a public no). post_001 energy: analytical, structural, not hedged mush, not boosterism, not manufactured criticism.

criteria.name: Forward implication
criteria.notes: Names a live, dated trigger (FERC comment/intervention window opened Sept 4, 2026) and concrete watch items. Specific rather than 'watch this space,' though presented as a list of possibilities rather than one crisp single trigger.

criteria.name: Voice match
criteria.notes: Analytical, business-literate, plain-language explanation of a regulatory mechanism, matching post_001's register. No hagiographic verbs, no press-release recap, no banned phrases. One mildly breezy turn ('the kind of load that math wants') is minor drift, not disqualifying.

criteria.name: Readability (LinkedIn)
criteria.notes: 449 body words and ~2,860 total characters both comfortably inside the windows. Two paragraphs ran 5-8 sentences each, longer than the tight 2-4 sentence target. ORCHESTRATOR NOTE: after scoring, those two paragraphs were split at sentence boundaries with no wording changed, addressing this exact point.

criteria.name: Engagement question
criteria.notes: Specific, debatable, tied directly to the decision's structural tension. No CTA, no rhetorical softener.

criteria.name: Credibility guard
criteria.notes: Bio recap minimal; decision treatment dominates word count. Both quotes verbatim matches to desk_dossier.json with correct source_url. Attribution honest and appropriately hedged rather than overclaiming independent confirmation of the rebuttal. Held back from 9-10 only because the post never signals that corroboration for Thayer's account is thinner than for the filing's existence.

hard_fails.note: Body plus hashtag line is under the 3,000-char cap.

hard_fails.name: subject_named_and_anchorage_tied
hard_fails.note: Curtis Thayer named with full name, title, and org; Anchorage tie stated explicitly.

hard_fails.name: recent_decision_named_with_primary_source
hard_fails.note: Decision dated 2026-08-19, within the 60-day window (on/after 2026-07-06); Anchorage Daily News named inline with the date.

hard_fails.name: multi_source_corroboration
hard_fails.note: The account of the underlying FERC filing is independently corroborated by the Federal Register notice per the dossier's corroborating_sources[].

hard_fails.name: grounded_not_press_release
hard_fails.note: Real analytical work, no hagiographic verbs, no recycled press-release language.
